# The intent folder (template)

> In ESOI, intents are meaningful containers of a set of specifications. For human understanding, they serve as a personal category of interest or relate to a tangible container such as an organization.

An intent is a folder. Its record is `intent.csv` (one row) and its specifications are the five record files beside it. The top intent is why the project exists, in the project's own words (it is custom to the project, never about ESOI unless ESOI is the project); the configured folder only holds it. The evolvable structure the project applies is a solution inside the top intent, whose implementation may use the esoi solutions. A sub-intent is a subfolder, named by its `intent_id`, that holds its own `intent.csv`; it arises as an implementation of a solution in the parent intent. Recording intents as folders is the selected implementation of the `intent-registry` solution; its rival, records kept beside the code they describe, stays a listed alternative, so the folder layout is one way to record the hierarchy, not the only one.

```
<folder>/                   holds the top intent
  intent.csv
  problems.csv  ideals.csv  solutions.csv  implementations.csv  metrics.csv
  <sub-intent-id>/          a sub-intent, in a folder named by its intent_id (its own intent.csv and five files)
```

## intent.csv

| Column | Filled by | Question or meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `intent_id` | you | A short stable id, unique across the tree. |
| `name` | you | What is a specific phrase which distinguishes the topic of the intent from other intents? |
| `vision_statement` | you | What is this intent manifesting in present tense? e.g. "I am ..." or "The world is ..." Any subject and verb can be used. |
| `opportunities` | you | What are potentials inspired by this intent? |
| `implements` | you | Sub-intent only: the full id of the parent intent's implementation it arises from (`<solution_id>:<name>`). Empty for the top intent. |

## What it is not

A general category like "parenting" or "career." An intent is also not an organization itself, rather the container of specification that clarifies why the organization exists (as a solution and implementation within an intent). In this example, different versions of the same organization can be documented as separate alternative implementations.

## The link from the parent

In the parent intent's `implementations.csv`, the implementation the sub-intent arises from names it back in `sub_intent`. An implementation that builds on solutions of other intents lists them in `uses_solution_ids`. Record ids are unique across the whole tree, so any link can name a record in another intent.

## When to add a sub-intent

Only when it brings insights on opportunities that do not emerge directly from the parent intent or the solution it implements; its `opportunities` cell states them (see [when to create a sub-intent](../explanation/when-to-create-a-sub-intent.md)). Risks belong in an implementation's or a metric's disadvantages and uncertainties in the solution's metric, so neither earns a sub-intent alone.
